variants.name: Sundown
variants.concept: A low sun sitting on the horizon with the clock hands knocked out at 5:00, so quitting time and the evening on the water are one shape. In the lockup the horizon is the wordmark baseline and the dial centre sits on the cap line.
variants.weaknesses: The flat-bottomed disc can read as a gauge or dome; the sun reading leans on the Sun/Rust thread. Like all four it lays down far more solid thread than the owner's quiet hands-only baseline.

variants.name: Nut
variants.concept: A hex nut seen from above, corners lightly chamfered like a machined nut, with the hands knocked out as a trades nod.
variants.weaknesses: The nut is implied only by the chamfered hexagon, so outside a trades context it can pass as a generic hexagonal clock badge.

variants.name: Ticket
variants.concept: An old admission ticket with punched-out corners and the hands knocked out: your ticket out.
variants.weaknesses: Concave-corner ticket frames are a familiar vintage-label trope, and the landscape shape leaves heavy solid areas either side of the upright hands.

variants.name: Label
variants.concept: A square woven label with the hands stitched in a contrast thread, the way a workwear tag is made; the one-colour file knocks the hands out.
variants.weaknesses: A clock in a square is the closest of the four to a generic clock or app icon, and the solid tile is the heaviest stitch area.
